subject.title: [Bug]: Unscheduled reminder guard fires for isolated-session crons + counter lost during compaction

question: Should maintainers adopt/refresh the conflicting full-fix fork PR, broaden/review the same-repo compaction PR, or open a same-repo replacement that fixes both reported gaps together?
rationale: The bug is source-proven, but there are overlapping open fix paths with different scope and mergeability, so automation should not create another duplicate repair branch before maintainers choose ownership and scope.

options.title: Replace With One Same-Repo Full Fix
options.body: Open or refresh a narrow target-repo PR that covers both isolated-cron matching and compaction-counter preservation with regression tests.

options.title: Land The Partial Compaction Fix First
options.body: Proceed with the same-repo compaction PR and keep this issue open for the isolated-session cron gap.

options.title: Wait On The Fork Refresh
options.body: Keep this issue paired with the fork PR and wait for the contributor to resolve conflicts, proof, and current-main drift.

recommendation.title: Replace With One Same-Repo Full Fix
recommendation.body: Open or refresh a narrow target-repo PR that covers both isolated-cron matching and compaction-counter preservation with regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the predecessor reminder-guard fix and recently maintained the affected auto-reply surfaces.
